title: Data Analyst Intern
description:
Portcast is a venture-backed, Singapore-based logistics technology startup building a real-time transportation visibility platform for global supply chains. We help shippers, manufacturers, and logistics service providers turn data into decisions and decisions into measurable business impact.
Our platform goes beyond visibility. Portcast enables action at scale by surfacing the right risks early, helping teams prevent detention and demurrage, accelerate exception management, and close invoices faster with built-in evidence. We turn visibility into outcomes: reduced costs, improved operational control, and more predictable supply chains.
Founded in 2018 and backed by leading technology investors, we are building for an industry at a critical inflection point of digital transformation. Our team of software engineers, data scientists, and logistics experts is on a mission to make supply chains not just visible, but decisively actionable: end to end.
## ABOUT THE ROLE:
Portcast runs on data, our engine predicts when, where, why, and by how many days a container will be delayed, and our customers trust those predictions to make actionable decisions. That trust depends on the data underneath being clean, connected, and reliable.
As our Data Analyst Intern, you'll join the Data team and work closely with our Data Analysts and Data Scientists, reporting to our Data Lead. Your focus will be on data integrations and quality, connecting new data sources into our system, checking the data we ingest for gaps and anomalies, and supporting the QA and automation work that keeps our predictions accurate. This is a hands-on learning role: you won't just be handed a checklist. When something in the data looks off, we'll want you to dig into why, not just flag it. Curiosity and effort matter more here than knowing everything already and exceptional A+ player interns have a real path to a permanent role.
## WHAT YOU'LL OWN:
Check ingested and system-generated data for anomalies and gaps, and help trace them to the source.
Help build and run QA checks, report generation, and automations using Python and SQL.
Assist the Data Analysts on day-to-day customer data queries and dashboard upkeep.
Support new data-source integrations, connecting carrier and market data into our system, with guidance from the team.
Document what you build and what you find, so the team can rely on and reuse your work.
## WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR:
Currently pursuing (Final-year student) or recently completed a degree in Computer Science, Data Analytics, Data Science, Engineering, Information Technology, Statistics, or a related field.
Working knowledge of Python and SQL, you don't need years of experience, but you should be able to write a query and a script and want to get sharper fast.
• Prior internship experience in a Data Analyst or Business Analyst role, preferably in a product-based, lean startup particularly in logistics, ecommerce or B2B SaaS data-heavy domain.
Willing to learn over "already knows everything": we hire interns for curiosity and effort. You put in the work to understand our domain, product, data, and customers.
Curious by Default: when the data surprises you, you chase the why. You ask good questions early and treat every gap as something worth understanding.
You own your output, AI included. You can use AI tools to move faster, but you read and validate what they produce, you don't just paste it. If one day the tool isn't there, you can still write the query yourself. You can explain what you did and why, without saying "the AI did it."
An eye for detail: you notice when a number looks wrong before anyone else does.
Empathy and urgency: you understand that clean data is what customers are counting on, and you move promptly day to day.
Fluent in written and verbal English, and comfortable working in a diverse, fully remote team.
## WHAT'S IN IT FOR YOU:
Real work from day one: you'll touch live data and integrations that customers actually depend on.
Mentorship: you'll learn directly from our Data Analysts and Data Scientists.
A path to permanent: strong & exceptional A+ player interns here have a real shot at converting to a full-time role.
Globally distributed, lean team remote-first flexibility: work with a fully distributed team across Asia and Europe, built on trust, accountability, and collaboration.
## Our CORE Values Guide Everything We Do:
Curiosity: We read the data before we trust it. We dig into why a number looks the way it does, not just how to make the anomaly disappear.
Ownership: We act like owners, not ticket-takers. We stay on a problem until it's actually fixed at the source.
Raising the bar: We don't settle for a report that only works this once. We aim for data pipelines and dashboards that are reliable, reusable, and easy for the team to trust.
Effectiveness: We focus on analysis that creates real product and customer impact. We prioritize the right problems, make practical trade-offs, and ship work that improves outcomes, not just output.
Join us at Portcast and be part of a high-performing team that is shaping the future of the logistics and shipping industry through cutting-edge predictive analytics!

description:
## Job Overview:
The Cambridge Computer Services HPC AI Network Technologist is a field-based consultant who builds end-to-end research computing system solutions focusing on networking design and implementation. The HPC AI Network Technologist is responsible for designing, implementing, and optimizing the network infrastructure that supports high-performance computing (HPC) and artificial intelligence (AI) workloads. You will leverage your expertise in scientific computing and knowledge of the technology landscape to drive outcomes that exceed client expectations.

• Gather client networking requirements, design optimized solutions, sometimes using a single vendor's portfolio and more often using a broad variety of vendors and technologies.

• Consult on and assist with day-to-day management of clients research computing infrastructure environments.

title: SQL/SSIS and Oracle Developer
description:
We are seeking a highly skilled SSIS / SQL Developer with proven expertise in data migration, particularly in migrating large-scale enterprise data from Oracle to Microsoft SQL Server. The ideal candidate will be responsible for designing, developing, and optimizing ETL pipelines using SQL Server Integration Services (SSIS), writing complex T-SQL queries, and ensuring data integrity throughout the migration lifecycle.
## KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
• Design, develop, and maintain robust SSIS packages for ETL workflows, data transformation, and automated data loads.
• Analyze Oracle database schemas, stored procedures, functions, and packages and re-engineer them in T-SQL for SQL Server compatibility.
• Develop complex T-SQL queries, stored procedures, views, triggers, and functions to support business logic and reporting requirements.
• Perform data profiling, cleansing, validation, and reconciliation to ensure accuracy and completeness during migration.
• Collaborate with business analysts, DBAs, and project managers to gather requirements and translate them into technical solutions.
• Conduct unit testing, integration testing, and performance tuning of ETL pipelines and SQL scripts.
• Document migration strategies, data mapping specifications, ETL workflows, and technical runbooks.
• Monitor and troubleshoot ETL job failures, data discrepancies, and performance bottlenecks in production and staging environments.
• Optimize SQL queries and SSIS packages for performance using indexing strategies, query plans, and execution profiling.
• Ensure compliance with data governance, security policies, and regulatory requirements throughout the migration process.
• Provide post-migration support, including issue resolution and performance monitoring.
## Requirements
## Core Technical Skills
• 5+ years of hands-on experience building and managing SSIS packages, including control flow, data flow, event handlers, and error handling.
• Strong proficiency in Microsoft SQL Server (2016/2019/2022), including T-SQL, query optimization, indexing, and database design.
• Solid experience working with Oracle (10g/11g/12c/19c), including PL/SQL, Oracle data types, sequences, and schema management.
• Proven experience executing Oracle-to-SQL Server migrations, including schema conversion, data mapping, and validation.
• Expertise in building scalable ETL pipelines for large datasets with strong data quality and transformation logic.
## Tools & Technologies
• Proficiency with SQL Server Management Studio (SSMS) and Visual Studio (SSDT).
• Proficiency with Oracle SQL Developer or TOAD.
• Experience with Microsoft SQL Server Migration Assistant (SSMA) for Oracle.
• Experience with SSIS Catalog and SQL Server Agent for job scheduling.
• Experience with Git, Azure DevOps, or TFS for version control is preferred.
• Experience with SSRS or Power BI for reporting integration is advantageous.
## PREFERRED / NICE-TO-HAVE QUALIFICATIONS
• Microsoft Certified: Azure Data Engineer Associate or an equivalent SQL Server certification.
• Experience with Azure Data Factory (ADF) or other cloud-based ETL platforms.
• Familiarity with data warehousing concepts, including star schema, snowflake schema, and slowly changing dimensions.
• Experience working with Azure cloud environments.
• Experience with Agile or Scrum methodologies.
• Experience with data lineage and metadata management tools.
## EDUCATIONAL REQUIREMENTS
• Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Software Engineering, or a related field is preferred.

title: Junior AI Consultant
description:
## Innovatie, elke dag
Maak kennis met Yellowtail Conclusion, dé IT Consultancy expert die al 20 jaar lang succesvolle IT-oplossingen biedt aan toonaangevende Nederlandse banken, verzekeraars, (semi)overheidsinstanties en financieel adviseurs. Wij hebben een bewezen staat van dienst in IT. Met innovatie in ons DNA en een gezond portie lef, gaan wij de uitdaging aan om Artificial Intelligence in de financiële wereld te integreren, en daar kunnen we jouw hulp goed bij gebruiken!
## Waarom is Junior AI Consultant jouw nieuwe job?
Als junior/medior AI consultant zal jij je in eerste instantie, zodra je start, zoveel mogelijk ontwikkelen op het vlak van IT en AI. Je bent betrokken bij het bouwen van IT-systemen en geeft daarbij richting aan developers. Hierdoor leer je terwijl je werkt, en zal je in staat zijn om technische en AI-gerelateerde concepten te vertalen naar begrijpelijke taal voor verschillende collega's binnen Yellowtail.
Je draagt daarnaast bij aan de interne ontwikkeling naar AI-gedreven werken. Dit doe je door het selecteren, maar ook onderzoeken, van geschikte AI tools en daar collega's over te onderwijzen. Je fungeert dan ook tegelijkertijd als vraagbaak. Hoewel je ambitie hebt om uiteindelijk zelf te bouwen, richt je je nu vooral op het aantonen en ontwikkelen van je kennis en begrip van IT en AI.
## Wie ben jij?
Je hebt een achtergrond in een relevante IT-opleiding, zoals computer science, informatica, data science of artificial intelligence. Je hebt ervaring met Azure en beschikt over inzicht in hoe frontend en backend met elkaar samenwerken. Je hebt een holistische kijk op IT en begrijpt hoe verschillende onderdelen zoals DevOps, hosting, netwerken, AI en applicatieontwikkeling samenhangen.
Je bent nieuwsgierig, gedreven, een meedenker en toont makkelijk initiatief. Daarbij kan het zijn dat je een AI-opleiding gecombineerd hebt met werkervaring in IT, of juist weer andersom. Je bent iemand die zich thuis voelt op het snijvlak van technologie en inhoud, en weet complexe vraagstukken helder over te brengen. Binnen ons team krijg je alle ruimte om je passie voor AI, IT en business consultancy verder te verdiepen en uit te bouwen, in een omgeving waar leren, experimenteren en impact maken centraal staan!
## Requirements
## Wat wij belangrijk vinden
Een afgeronde masteropleiding (WO) in een relevante studierichting. Denk aan computer science, wiskunde, data science, AI;
Je neemt 0 tot 2 jaar werkervaring met je mee (Artificial Intelligence of in de IT);
Sterke communicatievaardigheden in zowel Nederlands als Engels, op alle vlakken en niveaus, voor klanten en collega’s.
Je hebt een holistisch IT beeld; je snapt bijvoorbeeld hoe front-end en back-end met elkaar interacteren;
Je toont initiatief, bent nieuwsgierig naar nieuwe technologieën en vindt het leuk om jezelf hierin te blijven ontwikkelen.
## What’s in it for you?
Wij houden van duidelijkheid: de salarisrange voor deze functie is tussen € 3.000 en € 3.600. Daarnaast ontvang je een mobiliteitsvergoeding die je op een groene en verantwoorde manier mag inzetten (bijvoorbeeld door te kiezen voor een elektrische leaseauto).
Verder kun je erop rekenen dat alle basiszaken perfect geregeld zijn. Denk aan een goede lunch, een snelle MacBook, telefoon, een prima pensioenregeling en een soepele salaris- en kostenafhandeling.
Maar dat is nog lang niet alles! Wat ons écht onderscheidt is onze manier van werken:
Je mag volledig jezelf zijn en hoeft niet te voldoen aan een bepaald imago of stereotype. We zien je graag zoals je bent.
Je krijgt alle ruimte en kansen geboden om te groeien en te leren. Samen gaan we op zoek naar jouw talenten en ontwikkelen deze verder.
Je bepaalt grotendeels zelf waar en wanneer je werkt. Wij geloven in een goede werk-privé balans dus helpen we je om je thuiswerkplek goed en verantwoord in te richten. Maar we gaan verder: je kunt bij ons zelfs vanaf je favoriete vakantiebestemming remote werken!
Je kunt veel leuke activiteiten ondernemen met collega’s. Zo hebben we om het jaar een trip met het bedrijf of een Hackaton, elke maand een Cultural FriYay en regelmatig andere (sportieve, interessante, leerzame) evenementen.
En wil je op kantoor even een pauze nemen, kun je altijd je collega uitdagen voor een potje dart, tafelvoetbal of tafeltennis. Of je pakt de Yellowtail kantoorfiets voor een rondje Naarderbos!
## Highlights
Kickstart je carrière als AI Consultant bij Yellowtail Conclusion: ontwikkel jezelf, verdiep je (nog) verder in AI en leer complexe vraagstukken vertalen naar heldere, impactvolle oplossingen.

description:
## MERIDIAL
## SMB AI Power User — Competitive Evaluations
## Company
## Meridial
## Location
## Remote
## Engagement Type
## Independent Contractor
## About Meridial
Meridial places skilled, remote-first professionals into high-trust, high-precision operational opportunities for leading technology companies. Our teams work as an embedded extension of our clients' own product and operations organizations, holding the same quality bar and the same deadlines.
## The Opportunity
As an SMB AI Power User on the Competitive Evaluations team, you'll help a major consumer technology company find out where its bundled AI assistant subscription falls short of the standalone assistants small businesses already pay for. You are not an AI researcher studying the problem from the outside - you are a working or experienced business owner who already runs on these tools, and your own operations are the test bed.
Your day is spent doing what you already do: drafting ad copy, planning content, answering customer messages, researching suppliers, and reconciling numbers. The difference is that you do it across competing assistants, side by side, and document precisely where each one breaks. The failures you surface are the failures real paying subscribers will hit, which is exactly why the seat calls for a genuine operator rather than an evaluator.
## What You'll Do
• Run head-to-head prompts and multi-turn workflows across the client's assistant and competing paid assistants, using tasks drawn from your own business operations and marketing.
• Build and maintain a library of realistic small-business test cases spanning ad creative and copy, organic content planning, customer messaging, competitor research, pricing, scheduling, and light bookkeeping.
• Identify and document failure modes - wrong answers, unnecessary refusals, weak instruction-following, tone misses, brand-unsafe output, broken formatting, context lost across turns, unusable image or video output.
• Write clear, reproducible reports: prompt used, model and surface, expected output, actual output, severity, and why the failure matters to a paying business subscriber.
• Assess the bundled subscription on value terms - what a business owner actually receives versus what a standalone competitor subscription delivers for comparable spend.
• Stress-test assistant features inside the social and commerce surfaces where business owners meet them, not only the standalone chat product.
## What We're Looking For
• Owner or operator of a small or medium business - sole proprietor, founder, or the person running day-to-day operations at a business of roughly 1–200 employees.
• Daily, habitual use of generative AI tools in that business, for both operations and marketing. Experimental or occasional use is not a fit.
• Organic presence on Instagram and Facebook for the business, maintained personally: posting, Stories, Reels, comment and message response.
• Hands-on paid advertising experience on Meta platforms - has personally built, launched, and optimized campaigns with real budget.
• Based in the United States and authorized to work here.
• Capacity sufficient to complete deliverables per the agreed scope and timeline, which may include up to 40 hours per week
• Exceptional written English - able to describe a failure clearly enough that an engineer can reproduce it without follow-up.
• Comfortable working independently against a rubric and holding a weekly output cadence.
## Nice to Have
• At least one current paid AI subscription (ChatGPT Plus/Pro, Claude Pro/Max, Gemini Advanced, or similar), so competitive comparison rests on actual use.
• Runs a side business or second venture alongside a primary role - the profile that tends to test AI hardest against limited time.
• Heavy Instagram user, personally and commercially: fluent in Reels, Stories, trends, and creator tooling.
• Subscribes to two or more AI assistants simultaneously and holds an informed view on where each one wins.
• Uses AI beyond chat - automations, agents, API or no-code integrations, custom GPTs or Projects.
• Prior experience with model evaluation, red teaming, data annotation, QA, or structured user research.
• Working familiarity with adjacent SMB tooling: Shopify, Square, QuickBooks, Klaviyo, Canva, CapCut, Later, or similar.
• Industry range across the two hires - for example, one services or retail operator alongside one e-commerce or creator-economy operator.
We offer a pay range of $40-$50 per hour, with the exact rate determined after evaluating your experience, expertise, and geographic location. As a contractor you’ll supply a secure computer and high‑speed internet; company‑sponsored benefits such as health insurance and PTO do not apply.

title: AI Solutions Architect / Copilot Developer
description:
## AI Solutions Architect / Copilot Developer
Human-centered problem-solving meets Microsoft AI technology
## Role Overview
We're looking for someone who thinks like a strategist, debates like a philosopher, and builds like an engineer. This role sits inside our AI Solutions Group, where the individual will need to reason clearly about ambiguous problems, build consensus among stakeholders, and translate that thinking into working solutions on the Microsoft Power Platform.
You'll partner directly with clients to figure out where AI can provide tangible improvements, gather and interpret requirements (even when clients aren't sure what they need), build solutions using Power Platform tools, help test and validate what you've built, and keep it optimized over time. This role is about people, logic, and persuasion as much as it is about implementation.
## Why This Role Is Different
We believe the core skills for working effectively with AI aren't primarily technical. They're:
Creative problem solving: finding non-obvious paths through ambiguous, messy, or "less than optimal" situations
Strategic thinking: seeing the whole system, not just the ticket in front of you
Logic and structured reasoning: the same discipline that makes a good philosopher makes a good prompt engineer and a good solution architect
Communication and diplomacy: building consensus among stakeholders with competing priorities, teaching non-technical teams, and handholding through change
If you have a background in philosophy, strategy consulting, teaching, mediation, debate, logic, systems thinking, or similar disciplines, and you're excited by AI tools, we want to talk to you, even if your technical resume looks nontraditional.
## What You'll Actually Do
## With Clients
• Act as a trusted advisor: ask the right questions, challenge assumptions, and help clients articulate problems they haven't fully defined yet
• Build consensus across stakeholders with different, sometimes conflicting, priorities. This is often the hardest part of the job
• Teach and support end users through change, including patient handholding for less AI-fluent teams
• Translate business problems into technical requirements, and technical constraints back into plain language
## Building the Solution
• Design and develop solutions in Power Automate, Microsoft Copilot Studio, and related Power Platform tools
• When necessary, integrate adaptive cards, connectors, triggers, and APIs to extend functionality
• Craft effective prompts and grounding strategies for Copilot, Claude, and related AI tools. This is applied logic and language craft as much as coding
• Build and prototype using Copilot-related AI tools for development and automation, always within strict data-control guardrails
• Where possible, apply this same workflow to working with Anthropic’s Claude
## Keeping It Working
• Participate in testing, validation, and quality assurance
• Support ongoing maintenance, troubleshooting, and enhancement of deployed solutions
• Document decisions and create user guides that make adoption easier, not harder
• Escalate and resolve issues, mentoring teammates along the way
## Staying Sharp
• Continuously evaluate new AI tools and platforms, with a healthy respect for compliance, governance, and data protection in a regulated environment
• Bring an "AI mindset": curious, experimental, but never careless with sensitive data
## What We're Looking For
## Core (non-negotiable) skills:
• Strong critical thinking and structured reasoning: you can break down a fuzzy problem into a clear plan
• Excellent written and verbal communication, including the ability to present to and persuade skeptical or non-technical audiences
• Diplomacy and consensus-building, with comfort navigating disagreement without avoiding it
• A genuine curiosity about AI and a track record of picking up new tools quickly
• Comfort improvising solutions to non-technical problems, including political, organizational, or human friction, not just code bugs
## Technical qualifications:
• Bachelor's degree or real-world experience equivalent, any field, with philosophy, humanities, and social sciences welcome, and 3+ years of relevant professional experience
• Hands-on experience (or strong aptitude to quickly gain it) with Microsoft Power Platform (Power Apps, Power Automate, Dataverse) and Copilot Studio
• Familiarity with modern AI tools, especially Microsoft Copilot and Claude, including prompt engineering and LLM behavior
• Ability to work within a regulated environment with strict data controls, balancing experimentation against compliance
## Preferred:
• Background in strategy consulting, teaching, philosophy, logic, mediation/facilitation, or debate
• Understanding of Microsoft Graph API, REST APIs, and system integrations
• Experience with RAG-based architectures
• Certifications in Power Platform, AI, or Copilot-related specialties
• Experience with Agile/Scrum delivery
## Work Environment
Location: United States, Eastern Time Zone
Travel: None required
Schedule: Remote-first, asynchronous-friendly, with some real-time overlap for meetings and collaboration
## The Bigger Picture
This is a strategic development role on a high-performing team helping organizations reimagine how they work with AI, using Microsoft Power Platform, Copilot, Claude, and beyond. The technology moves fast, and we have a need for people who can think clearly, communicate persuasively, and navigate ambiguity with grace. If that's you, let’s talk.

• Opportunity to develop and advance within a growing organization

title: Research Scientist Intern (PhD) - Cohort '27
description:
## Who we are
Foundation models transformed text and images. Structured data - the largest and most consequential data format in the world - stayed untouched, until now. What LLMs did for language, we're doing for tables.
We pioneered tabular foundation models: TabPFN v2 was a Nature cover story, has passed 3.5M+ downloads and 7,500+ GitHub stars, and runs in production from detecting lung disease with Oxford Cancer Analytics to preventing train failures with Hitachi. The hardest problems - millions of rows, real-time inference, entirely new modalities - are still open, and no one else is working on them at this level.
We're a small, highly selective team of 40+ with backgrounds from Google, DeepMind, Meta, Apple, Amazon, Jane Street, and CERN, led by Frank Hutter, Noah Hollmann, and Sauraj Gambhir, and advised by Bernhard Schölkopf and Turing Award winner Yann LeCun.
In July 2026, less than 18 months after our €9M pre-seed, we joined SAP as an independent frontier AI lab - same team, mission, and open-weights models, now backed by more than €1 billion over four years.
About the role
You’ll join our research team for a 4 to 6 month internship, in the cohort that starts in May 2027. The work is hands-on, with tabular foundation models, a new class of AI model, and how they’re applied. We have more open research problems than people to work on them, and you’ll get a project matched to your interests and expertise, with the chance to publish the results. Some of the problems we’re working on:
Scaling model architectures and training
Models that read text and tables together
Architectures for time series, forecasting and anomaly detection
Faster training and inference
Causal reasoning in foundation models
Learning across multiple related tables
Benchmarks that show where tabular foundation models work and where they break, in science and in industry
What we’re looking for
You’re doing a PhD in computer science, applied maths, statistics, electrical engineering or a related field.
You have at least one first-author or shared-first-author paper at a top venue such as NeurIPS, ICML or ICLR.
You've turned your own research ideas into working experiments, for example in PyTorch, and you can tell when code is quietly wrong, whether you or a coding agent wrote it.
You can join us in Freiburg or Berlin from May 2027 for 4 to 6 months.
Experience with data science for tabular data or time series data is a plus
Mentorship at Prior Labs
Your mentor will be one of the researchers building TabPFN, who’ll help you with the technical side of your project and with your development as a researcher. Before you accept, we agree on a project area and a mentor with you, so you know what you’re working on and who you’re working with from day one. During the internship you’ll also work alongside the rest of our research and data science teams.
Benefits
A cohort of PhD interns who start with you, and a week-long workshop in Freiburg with the whole cohort in summer 2027
Opportunity to publish your work
Compute for your project
Healthcare, transportation and fitness covered
Key dates
Applications close on 1 January 2027. We review applications as they arrive, so applying early helps.
The cohort starts on 1 May 2027 with a joint onboarding. We can make exceptions, but we’d like you to start with the cohort.
The internship lasts 4 to 6 months, with 6 preferred.
## Life at Prior Labs
You'll work alongside researchers and builders who hold themselves to a very high bar - in the quality of their work and in how they work with each other. We move fast and still take the time to do things right.
Our teams are based in Berlin, Freiburg, and New York - when you're working on something as hard as TabPFN, being in the same room matters. But great people come from everywhere, and in exceptional cases we're open to remote, which usually means frequent travel to one of our offices. Wherever you're based, the whole company comes together regularly for offsites to build and celebrate together.
## Our Commitments
The best products and teams are built by people with a wide range of perspectives and backgrounds. We welcome applications from all identities and walks of life - especially if you've ever felt discouraged by "not checking every box" - and provide equal opportunities regardless of gender, sexual orientation, origin, disability, or any other trait that makes you who you are.
We care about how your data is handled - see our Recruiting Data Privacy page

That is what quinn is building, and it is further along than most people assume: a profitable core business, running today in Switzerland, Germany and the UK, expanding into new markets both by launching and by acquiring. By 2030 quinn intends to be the destination brand for fair employment across six countries and more, on one platform, with one experience.
One platform means one frontend. One experience means it looks and behaves like quinn whether you are in Zurich or in London, a household or a company. In this strategy that is not a nice-to-have. It is the strategy.
Which is why the surface matters more than anything else. Everything quinn does is designed to disappear. The interface is the only part the customer ever sees, and it is the whole proof that the complexity behind it is really handled.
Why this role exists
Today, quinn runs on several separate web apps: one per product and market, each with its own frontend, grown over the years as the company grew. Our backend engineers built them alongside everything else, plus an internal admin tool that grew the same way. They all work: thousands of employers run payroll through them every month. But nobody was ever tasked with owning the frontend development, so each one got built the way frontend is built by Backend Developers, seen as a hassle rather than the main aspect users interactive with.
What comes next is one frontend that replaces all of them, built from scratch: one quinn app for employers, employees and our own support team, in the browser first, then in the App Store and Google Play from the same work. Alongside it, the frontend of Maestro, the internal tool that replaces the old admin for batch processes. The phone app is the surface that matters most, so everything is built for it from the first screen rather than adapted to it afterwards.
That is the opening.
How we work
We are AI-native, and we mean it operationally rather than as a slogan. AI is how the work gets done here. It is why a small team ships like a large one, and it is a large part of how one person will be able to hold the standard we are describing.
We expect you to be at the front of that. Not to have heard of the tools, to live in them, and to build your own leverage with them: scaffolding, visual regression checks, design-token pipelines, whatever takes manual work out of the way.
And we expect the judgement that has to come with it. AI writes code that looks right and is subtly wrong: structure that doesn't scale, patterns that fall apart three screens later, components that work once and never again. You take the speed and throw away the rest. AI never lowers the bar here. It is the reason the bar can be this high.
## Tasks
What you will own
Everything on the screen:
• The frontend of the quinn app and the web app. App first. One app for everyone who uses quinn: the employer, the employee, and our own support team working inside the customer's account.
• The frontend of Maestro, our internal batch tool. Desktop and dense: queues, runs, tables, filters, multi-select, keyboard shortcuts. A different discipline from the app, built on the same components.
• The component library across quinn Home and quinn Business: one frontend, one experience, every market and every device.
• Whether the app feels native: response, scrolling, gestures, transitions, biometric login, push. Nothing that gives away it isn't native.
• The quality of what you ship. Nothing leaves your hands half-finished.
Where design ends, engineering begins.
We have a design team, and they own how quinn looks and behaves: the flows, the visual design, the tokens, the component specs. You don't design. You own everything from there: how it is built, and everything a design file cannot reasonably specify, such as gestures, keyboard, safe areas, what happens between the drawn breakpoints, the loading, offline, pending and failed states, what a three-line German label does to a layout that was designed for English. You are in the room before design starts, saying what already exists in the library and what a new pattern costs. Not at the end, receiving a handover. When you and design disagree, they decide how it looks and behaves and you decide how it is built. Nothing enters the component library without both of you.
## Requirements
Who we are looking for
You care about interfaces more than anyone else in the room. You see the two-pixel misalignment without being told, and it bothers you until it is fixed.
You build and maintain UI components and design systems, not one-off screens. You can build a mobile app that feels like one. And you can also build a desktop tool full of tables, filters and keyboard shortcuts, because Maestro is one. You understand UX and how people actually behave, not only how a screen looks. And you write code other people can take over: scalable, structured, documented. Not something that only works while you are in the building.
You are independent and decisive. Nobody will spec every detail for you and nobody will review your pixels.
You are fluent in English, no other language is required. And if you have a portfolio, a live product, or anything you have shipped that you are proud of, show it to us. Not a requirement, but it tells us more than a CV does.
Most importantly: you want this one. Not a frontend role at a company where the frontend is a chore. This one, the app nobody has built yet, the standard nobody has set yet, and a company where getting it right actually decides whether the strategy works.
The Team
We are a small, fast, direct team. We do not have a lot of process or a lot of hierarchy. We do have a clear strategy, an ambitious plan, and five values we actually mean: Be open, Own it, Speak up, Keep it simple, Bias for action.
This is one of the most important hires we will make this year. We are not rushing it and we are not filling a seat. We are looking for the person who reads this and thinks: finally.

title: Mainframe Data Engineer - 3 to 6 Months Contract
description:
We are seeking an experienced Senior Data Engineer with a strong background in designing, deploying, configuring, and managing enterprise-scale data engineering platforms within secure, on-premises and air-gapped environments.
The ideal candidate will have extensive hands-on experience working with Apache Hadoop and Apache Spark clusters, including installation, configuration, administration, troubleshooting, performance optimisation, and workload management in environments with restricted or no internet connectivity.
This role will support our Global Data Centre (GDC) environment, requiring a candidate who understands the operational and technical challenges of delivering robust, scalable, and secure data platforms within isolated infrastructure.
The successful candidate will work closely with infrastructure, platform, DevOps, and data engineering teams to build and maintain reliable data processing capabilities.
## Key Responsibilities
• Design, deploy, configure, and maintain Apache Hadoop and Apache Spark clusters in on-premises and air-gapped environments.
• Manage the full lifecycle of Hadoop/Spark platforms, including installation, upgrades, patching, configuration, monitoring, and troubleshooting.
• Develop, implement, and maintain scalable data pipelines for batch and distributed data processing.
• Optimise Spark workloads and Hadoop cluster performance, including resource allocation, job scheduling, and capacity management.
• Work with PostgreSQL and other enterprise data systems to support data integration, storage, and processing requirements.
• Support the deployment and management of containerised applications using Kubernetes and Helm.
• Implement and manage service-to-service communication and traffic management using Istio Service Mesh.
• Ensure software dependencies, container images, packages, and platform components can be deployed and maintained without external internet connectivity.
• Implement secure configuration and operational practices aligned with enterprise security requirements.
• Troubleshoot complex infrastructure, cluster, application, and data pipeline issues.
• Collaborate with infrastructure, security, DevOps, and application teams to ensure platform stability and availability.
• Maintain technical documentation, deployment procedures, operational runbooks, and platform architecture documentation.
• Support integration with legacy enterprise data systems, including VSAM.
Requirements
## Required Technical Skills & Experience
1. Apache Hadoop & Apache Spark
• Strong hands-on experience deploying, configuring, and administering Apache Hadoop clusters.
• Proven experience deploying and managing Apache Spark clusters and workloads.
• Experience with distributed data processing, batch processing, and large-scale data pipelines.
• Strong understanding of cluster architecture, resource management, performance tuning, and troubleshooting.
• Experience operating big data platforms in on-premises and air-gapped environments.
2. Air-Gapped & On-Premises Infrastructure
• Practical experience working in isolated, restricted-network, or air-gapped environments.
• Understanding of offline software installation, dependency management, package repositories, and container image management.
• Experience managing platform deployments without direct access to public internet repositories.
• Knowledge of secure infrastructure operations and enterprise deployment standards.
3. Containerisation & Platform Engineering
• Experience with Kubernetes-based platform deployments.
• Hands-on experience with Helm charts for application and platform deployments.
• Working knowledge of Istio Service Mesh, including traffic management, service discovery, and secure service-to-service communication.
• Understanding of container orchestration and microservices architecture.
4. Data Systems & Engineering
• Strong experience with PostgreSQL, including database integration and performance considerations.
• Experience designing, developing, and maintaining data pipelines.
• Understanding of distributed data storage and processing architectures.
• Knowledge of VSAM and integration with legacy enterprise data environments.
## Preferred / Desirable Skills
• Experience supporting large-scale enterprise or government data centre environments.
• Familiarity with Linux system administration.
• Experience with infrastructure automation and configuration management.
• Knowledge of data security, access controls, encryption, and secure data handling.
• Experience with monitoring, logging, and platform observability.
• Exposure to DevOps and CI/CD practices in restricted-network environments.
## Candidate Profile
The ideal candidate will be a hands-on technical engineer rather than purely an architectural or theoretical resource. They should be comfortable taking ownership of the deployment, administration, troubleshooting, and ongoing operational management of Hadoop and Spark platforms.
Candidates must be able to demonstrate practical experience working within environments where internet connectivity is restricted or unavailable, with an understanding of the additional complexities involved in deploying and maintaining enterprise data platforms in such environments.

title: Software Engineer II: Autonomous Supply Chains
description:
About Flexport: 

At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year. 

The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.

Applied AI Engineer, Autonomous Supply Chains

About Flexport

Look around you. Almost everything in the room crossed an ocean to get there. Moving one container from a factory to a warehouse takes 10 to 15 companies: truckers, customs brokers, port terminals, ocean carriers, insurers, lenders and warehouses, each with its own systems, paperwork and rules. A freight forwarder runs that whole journey, so the brand that makes the goods doesn't have to.

Most forwarders still run it on email, spreadsheets and phone calls. We call it email freight forwarding. Flexport runs it on one platform, where AI agents do the routine work and experts step in where judgment matters. We've moved $175B of goods for more than 13,000 brands across 135 countries. Our agents handle 21 million tasks a year, and up to 80% of customs work is automated.

Global logistics is a $13 trillion industry, and even the largest forwarder earns less than 3% of global logistics outsourcing revenue. People-powered operations don't scale: to grow, you hire. Software broke that ceiling for taxis with Uber, and for payments with Adyen and Stripe. Freight is next.

Amsterdam is one of Flexport's six engineering hubs, alongside San Francisco, Seattle, Chicago, Shanghai and Shenzhen. We own four domains end to end: Customs Technology, Autonomous Supply Chains (Applied AI), Platform and Security. See what we build at amsterdam-engineering.flexport.com.

The team: Autonomous Supply Chains

Logistics is famously hard to automate, because the happy path rarely happens. One customer won't take deliveries on a Tuesday. Another wants invoices only on Fridays, with some lines merged and others renamed. Until recently, people handled all of that by hand. Now operators use Forge, the agentic platform we build, to automate their own work: catching anomalies, routing exceptions, escalating stuck containers and adjusting invoices to each customer. Forge remembers every customer's rules and learns from every workflow run, so it gets smarter every day.

Autonomous Supply Chains is our Applied AI team: small, senior and reporting to the VP of Engineering. Self-driving cars are rated from level 0 to level 5. Most of the freight industry still runs at level 0: people emailing spreadsheets. Our goal is level 5 for freight, with Forge as the best agentic platform there is, handling every complexity, every calamity and every odd preference without skipping a beat.

Stack: TypeScript, Rust, Next.js, Temporal, Postgres and Snowflake, with models from Anthropic, OpenAI and Google.

The role

As an Applied AI Engineer II on Autonomous Supply Chains, you'll build the agents and AI-powered applications that make Flexport's operations faster and increasingly autonomous. You'll find the most painful problems in our operations, design the solution and ship it to operators moving freight across 135 countries. This isn't a role where you join a team and pick up tickets.

What you'll do

  • Design and ship end-to-end AI agents that handle real logistics work, such as customs compliance, document processing, invoice validation and exception management.
  • Build the evaluation, guardrails and human-in-the-loop flows that make an agent trustworthy enough to run 24/7.
  • Stay on top of what's happening in the world of AI, and channel those innovations straight into the product. When Jev came out this fall, we had three use cases live within two weeks.
  • Work directly with operators, domain experts and leadership to turn ambiguous problems into shipped products, and measure whether they worked.
  • Move fast from idea to production, and treat every deployment as a chance to learn.
  • Cross organizational boundaries to understand problems deeply and get things done without waiting for permission.

You should have

  • 3+ years of software engineering experience, and you've built seriously with LLMs, whether in production, in side projects or just because you couldn't stop yourself.
  • LLM fluency: agent patterns, tool use, RAG, prompt design and evaluation. You know the difference between what works in production and what looks good in a demo.
  • Full-stack capability in TypeScript and Next.js. You can own a feature end to end.
  • Product instinct: you can tell what's worth building, not just how to build it.
  • Clear written and spoken communication in English, including design docs that people actually read.

Nice to have

  • Experience with workflow orchestration, such as Temporal.
  • Experience building internal tools or operator-facing applications.

How we work

  • We value builders. People who think end to end, do their own discovery and ship independently. Nobody hands you a spec.
  • Your users sit next to you. Operators, customs experts and account teams work in the same office. Watch them use your tool, and fix it before dessert.
  • Any model, any harness. Use any frontier model from Anthropic, OpenAI or Google, in all the popular coding harnesses. Our engineers manage swarms of coding agents from their first week.
  • We ship dozens of times a day, with continuous deployment and a platform team obsessed with making it safe and fast.
  • Hybrid, in English. We're together in our office on Nieuwezijds Voorburgwal, a few minutes from Dam Square, three days a week*. The other days are flexible. English is our working language, and we work daily with colleagues in the US and China.
  • No logistics background needed. Almost nobody joins knowing what an HTS code or a bill of lading is. The experts sit a few desks away.
  • Agile, but not dogmatic. Teams decide how they work best.

Why this role is special

  • Your work is visible: a small, senior team that reports to the VP of Engineering. What you build gets noticed, and your ideas shape the direction.
  • Real stakes: your agents act on real shipments for 13,000+ brands in 135 countries, so the impact is immediate and measurable.
  • You're early: the playbook for applied AI in logistics hasn't been written yet. You'll help write it.

What's in it for you

  • Equity for everyone: every team member becomes a shareholder in a pre-IPO company in a multi-trillion dollar industry.
  • 25 vacation days, based on full-time employment, plus Dutch public holidays.
  • Health insurance, fully paid: a collective plan with basic and additional packages. Flexport pays the monthly premium.
  • Pension: a defined contribution scheme.
  • Breakfast and lunch: daily catered lunch with vegetarian options, breakfast, snacks and drinks in the office.
  • Commute covered: Flexport covers home-to-office commuting costs if you live outside Amsterdam.
  • Parental leave: time off for both parents to bond with a new child.
  • Wellbeing support: an Employee Assistance Program through Aetna for you and your household, at no cost.
  • Visa sponsorship: we sponsor visas for the right candidates and help you move to Amsterdam. Eligible international hires may also benefit from the Dutch expat tax ruling.

Our hiring process

  1. Application review: our team reviews your application.
  2. Recruiter screen: talk about your experience, the role and your questions about Flexport.
  3. Remote coding: your first coding interview takes place over video.
  4. Onsite coding and system design: a second coding interview and system design in our office.
  5. Project deep dive: discuss a project from your experience with the hiring manager.
  6. Team debrief: the interview team reviews feedback together. You don't attend this step.
  7. Offer: if there's a match, your recruiter walks you through the offer.

An additional remote coding round may be needed if the earlier coding interviews leave questions to resolve. Your recruiter will confirm the plan before interviews begin. We only contact candidates from ----- addresses, and we will never ask you for money or banking details.

At Flexport, our ability to fulfill our mission of making global commerce easy and accessible relies on having a diverse, dedicated and engaged workforce. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, physical and mental disability, health status, marital and family status, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, military and veteran status, and any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

title: Backend Engineer
description:
At Catawiki, every day brings the extraordinary! Whether it’s Daniel Ricciardo’s Formula 1 Car, a Woolly Mammoth’s Skeleton, Lady Gaga's Jumpsuit or Usain Bolt’s running shoe, we encounter exceptional objects every day.

We’re a one-of-a-kind marketplace for buying and selling special objects. Each week, more than 100,000 unique items are auctioned, all carefully curated by our passionate in-house experts.

Having sold over 25 million unique objects, our mission is to become the world’s most popular destination for special objects. As a growing, diverse and sustainable scale-up, we proudly live by three core values. If these values resonate with you, we’d love to explore how you can join us.

  • Taking ownership and driving impact 
  • Being open to change and feedback
  • Being passionate about our mission and our customers. 

Your Mission

On our path to becoming the most visited online curated marketplace for special objects, our Engineering team is on a mission to deliver the best experience across our platforms by building best-in-class products for search and discovery, bidding, curation, logistics, payments, and support.

We’re a scale-up tackling customer-facing challenges at high scale, with 75,000 auctions per week and more than 10 million visitors per month. As a Backend Engineer, you’ll support one of our three verticals - Demand, Supply, or Fulfilment - improving and delivering product innovations for our platform.
Working in a small, fully autonomous, and highly collaborative Agile team, you will build scalable, maintainable, and resilient microservices and features. That’s why we’re looking for developers who share ideas, explore options, and communicate openly.

What You'll Do

You’ll be part of a team with end-to-end responsibility for its own microservices, collaborating across disciplines to build, operate, and continuously improve our products.

  • Build end-to-end by designing, developing, testing, deploying, maintaining, and improving scalable microservices and features.
  • Own what you deliver, taking responsibility for the quality, resilience, and maintainability of your team’s services throughout their lifecycle.
  • Collaborate across disciplines while closely working with product designers, product owners, and frontend, backend, and mobile engineers to share ideas and deliver product innovations.
  • Improve how we work, identifying opportunities to make our engineering processes more effective and efficient.
  • Strengthen our engineering culture by documenting and advocating for development best practices across the team.
  • Raise product quality by fixing bugs and refactoring the codebase where necessary to keep our products reliable and maintainable.
  • Learn and experiment by testing new technologies and participating in Technical Week - a week dedicated to creativity, innovation, and knowledge sharing across domains after every two product sprints.

What You'll Bring

You understand the full lifecycle of web development, identify opportunities, explore solutions, and keep customer needs at the center of your work. Our stack is mainly focused on Ruby; however, prior Ruby experience is not essential if you’re passionate about learning new things.

  • Strong software engineering foundations: 7+ years of software development experience, specifically with object-oriented programming.
  • Relevant product experience: 3+ years of experience working with customer-facing products in industries such as e-commerce, fintech, or SaaS.
  • Backend service expertise: Experience designing, implementing, and deploying backend services with a focus on high availability, low latency, and consistency.
  • API and data knowledge: A good understanding of API design, SQL, and relational databases.
  • Clear communication: Excellent English communication skills and comfort raising concerns, sharing ideas, and documenting your work.
  • Collaborative mindset: You contribute to the team, take initiative, and step in to help when needed.
  • Solution-oriented thinking: You actively identify opportunities and explore alternative approaches to solving problems.
  • Commitment to growth: You take ownership of developing your skills by learning new technologies and seeking new opportunities.

How We Work

Our engineers work in small, fully autonomous, and highly collaborative Agile teams aligned with one of three verticals: Demand, Supply, or Fulfilment.

  • Teams are responsible for their own microservices from design and development through deployment, maintenance, and improvement.
  • Engineers collaborate closely with product designers, product owners, and frontend, backend, and mobile colleagues.
  • We value bold thinking, curiosity, openness, initiative, and a strong customer focus.
  • Technical Week creates dedicated space for experimentation, creativity, innovation, and knowledge sharing across domains.

Where You'll Be

This is a Hybrid role based in Amsterdam. You will work from our Amsterdam HQ a minimum of 2 days per week.
At this time, we are only considering candidates who are already based in the Netherlands. As a result, relocation support is not available for this position. We can, however, provide visa transfer from current Dutch employer.

In Return

You’ll be part of an enthusiastic, highly motivated team of 800+ Catawikians.

  • A competitive Annual Gross Base Salary depending on your level, competencies, and overall experience.
  • A Work From Home Allowance to help with your monthly household bills.
  • Commuting between your home and our office is covered by Catawiki.
  • Amazing Office right in the centre of Amsterdam.

Why You'll Love Working with Us

  • Create a visible impact by working at scale in a global organisation serving millions of customers across 80+ categories. In our flat structure, every role has a broad scope and directly impacts both our customers and the business.
  • Learn and grow through our Learning & Development initiatives, including clear development plans and mentorship programmes to support your career progression.
  • A culture of connection defines us. We’re a passionate, diverse team of 800+ Catawikians representing 60+ nationalities. We foster an inclusive and queer-friendly environment where everyone is encouraged to bring their full self to work.
  • Celebrate life’s moments with us. You’ll receive a €100 Catavoucher when you join, a €50 Catavoucher on your birthday, and an extra day off each year to “Pursue Your Passion”. We also offer additional leave for key work anniversaries and important life events. Benefits may vary by location.

Our Offices and Way of Working

Junior Software Engineer (m/w/d) Top Tier Team
Research Engineer, AI-enabled Fusion Plasma Diagnostics (FEAT)
description:
The FEAT Centre is seeking a Research Engineer to develop AI-enabled approaches for fusion plasma diagnostics and data analysis. The work spans two closely connected areas: fusion diagnostics and data analysis, and AI model development, with flexibility to focus on either area or work across both.
## Who we are looking for
The FEAT Centre is seeking a Research Engineer to contribute to the use of experimental diagnostics and AI for fusion plasma research. You will work with diverse experimental data from fusion plasma diagnostics, including microwave, imaging, and other measurement techniques, to develop new approaches for plasma analysis and interpretation. The research presents opportunities to develop AI methods that learn across heterogeneous measurements and experimental devices while incorporating knowledge of the underlying physics.
This position is part of the Plasma Physics and Diagnostics Department (PPDD), which hosts expertise in plasma modelling and diagnostics. You will work closely with plasma physicists, diagnostic scientists, and AI researchers, and collaborate with international partners across universities and fusion research facilities.
The research covers two complementary technical tracks:
1. Fusion diagnostics and data analysis: Analyse and interpret experimental diagnostic data, including signal processing, data curation, diagnostic reconstruction, validation, and the development of robust analysis workflows.
2. AI model development: Develop machine-learning methods for fusion diagnostic data, including multimodal and time-series modelling, representation learning, forecasting, transfer learning, and physics-informed approaches.
Depending on your expertise, you may contribute primarily to one track or work across both. You will contribute to publications and collaborative research projects, and help develop FEAT's capabilities in AI-enabled plasma diagnostics.
## What you'll be doing
Develop and apply computational methods for the analysis and interpretation of fusion plasma diagnostic data.
Process, curate, and analyse experimental datasets from multiple diagnostics and fusion devices.
Develop and evaluate machine-learning models for diagnostic analysis, reconstruction, classification, and forecasting.
Develop and apply AI approaches for learning from heterogeneous scientific data and transferring models across fusion devices.
Develop scalable and reproducible analysis and machine-learning workflows using GPU and high-performance computing resources.
Collaborate with internal teams and international research partners, contribute to publications, and support collaborative projects.
## What you'll bring
Must-Haves
Bachelor's or Master's degree in Physics, Engineering, Computer Science, Machine Learning, Applied Mathematics, Computational Science, or a closely related field.
Strong background in at least one of the following areas: plasma or experimental physics, scientific data analysis, machine learning, or scientific computing.
Strong numerical and data-analysis skills, with proficiency in scientific programming (e.g., Python, C/C++, Julia).
Experience working with experimental, simulation, or other complex scientific datasets.
Strong written and spoken English communication skills, with the ability to work effectively in interdisciplinary teams.
Good-to-Haves
Background in plasma physics, fusion science, plasma diagnostics, or experimental physics.
Experience with diagnostic or scientific data analysis, including signal processing, time-series analysis, imaging, or inverse problems.
Experience developing machine-learning models using frameworks such as PyTorch, JAX, or TensorFlow.
Experience with areas such as multimodal learning, representation learning, self-supervised learning, foundation models, forecasting, transfer learning, or uncertainty quantification.
Experience with scientific or physics-informed machine learning.
Experience with high-performance computing, GPU acceleration, or large-scale computational workflows.
## What you'll need to succeed
Scientific problem-solving and critical thinking
Initiative and willingness to learn
Research communication (written and oral)
Collaboration and teamwork in interdisciplinary environments
## What we offer
Opportunity to develop AI and diagnostic methods for challenging problems in fusion plasma research.
Access to experimental datasets from international fusion research programmes and advanced GPU and high-performance computing resources.
Close collaboration with plasma physicists, diagnostic scientists, AI researchers, and international fusion research partners.
Flexibility to pursue research in fusion diagnostics and data analysis, AI model development, or across both areas.
Apply now
